note: Biology round 4: two data passages (exercise/pulse table, dihybrid pea cross) and applied items across all fifteen topics, taking Biology past 500 curated questions.

passages.title: Pulse and breathing rate of a student before and after exercise
passages.text:
A student's pulse rate and breathing rate
were recorded at rest, during light and
heavy exercise, and during recovery. The
results are shown below.

Activity              Pulse  Breaths
                      (/min)  (/min)
Resting                 72      15
Walking for 5 min       95      20
Running for 5 min      150      38
2 min after running    120      30
10 min after running    78      16

passages.title: Results of a cross between two pea plants
passages.text:
A plant breeder crossed two pea plants
that were both heterozygous for seed shape
(round R, wrinkled r) and seed colour
(yellow Y, green y). The 556 seeds
produced were sorted as shown below.

Type of seed          Number
Round, yellow          315
Round, green           108
Wrinkled, yellow       101
Wrinkled, green         32

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: From the table above, the percentage increase in the student's pulse rate between resting and running is approximately

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the experiment above, the breathing rate rose during running in order to
questions.A: cool the body by breathing out warm air
questions.B: slow down the heart so that it does not tire
questions.C: reduce the amount of water lost from the lungs
questions.D: supply oxygen faster and remove carbon(IV) oxide faster
questions.explanation: Working muscles respire faster, so more oxygen must be taken in and more carbon(IV) oxide removed per minute.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the experiment above, the pulse rate was still high two minutes after the student stopped running because
questions.A: the heart takes a long time to receive the message to slow down
questions.B: the student was still frightened by the exercise
questions.C: the blood had become too thick to flow quickly through the veins
questions.D: oxygen was still needed to break down the lactic acid built up in the muscles
questions.explanation: During hard exercise muscles respire partly anaerobically; the oxygen debt is repaid after exercise, so heart and breathing rates stay raised.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: From the table above, the reading that shows the student had almost fully recovered is
questions.explanation: Ten minutes after running the pulse (78) and breathing rate (16) are close to the resting values of 72 and 15.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During the run in the experiment above, the student's leg muscles were short of oxygen. The substance that accumulated in them was
questions.explanation: In animals, anaerobic respiration converts glucose to lactic acid, which causes fatigue and cramp.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The rise in pulse rate during exercise in the experiment above is brought about by
questions.A: the hormone insulin acting on the heart muscle
questions.B: an increase in the number of red blood cells
questions.C: the lungs pumping blood faster through the heart
questions.D: nerve impulses and the hormone adrenaline acting on the heart
questions.explanation: The sympathetic nerves and adrenaline speed up the pacemaker, raising the heart rate and the force of contraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The results in the table above are closest to the ratio
questions.explanation: 315 : 108 : 101 : 32 divided by about 35 gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, the classic dihybrid ratio.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: From the results above, the dominant characters are
questions.explanation: The commonest phenotypes show the dominant traits: round shape and yellow colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The genotype of each parent plant in the cross above was
questions.explanation: Both parents were heterozygous for both characters (dihybrid), which is the only cross that gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: From the table above, the number of wrinkled green seeds expected from 556 seeds is about
questions.explanation: 1/16 of 556 = 34.75, i.e. about 35, close to the 32 observed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The cross above illustrates Mendel's law of
questions.explanation: Seed shape and seed colour were inherited independently of each other, producing all four combinations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Of the round yellow seeds in the table above, the fraction expected to be pure-breeding (RRYY) is
questions.explanation: Nine genotype boxes give round yellow; only one of them (RRYY) is homozygous for both, so 1/9.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A drop of pond water viewed under the microscope shows a colourless cell with no cell wall and an outline that keeps changing shape as it moves. The organism is most likely
questions.explanation: Amoeba moves and feeds by pushing out temporary pseudopodia, so its shape is never fixed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A student's drawing of a cell measures 60 mm across. If the actual cell is 30 µm wide, the magnification of the drawing is

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a student changes from the low-power to the high-power objective of a microscope, the area of the specimen seen
questions.explanation: Higher magnification shows a smaller part of the specimen, and less light passes through the narrower lens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell that makes and secretes large amounts of digestive enzymes would be expected to contain many
questions.C: ribosomes and a well-developed Golgi body
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins made on ribosomes and packaged for secretion by the Golgi body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mitochondria are described as the power houses of the cell because they
questions.A: store starch for use during famine
questions.B: make the proteins that the cell needs
questions.C: control all the activities of the cell
questions.D: release energy from food by aerobic respiration
questions.explanation: Most of the ATP used by a cell is produced in its mitochondria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A visking tubing containing strong sugar solution was tied and placed in a beaker of water. After an hour it was swollen and firm. This happened because
questions.A: sugar diffused out of it into the water through its wall
questions.B: it absorbed the sugar and expanded as the sugar dissolved
questions.C: water entered it by osmosis through its partially permeable wall
questions.D: air entered it through tiny holes in the wall of the tubing
questions.explanation: Water passes from the dilute solution (pure water) through the membrane into the concentrated sugar solution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A group of similar cells performing the same function, such as the cells lining the cheek, is called
questions.explanation: Cells → tissues → organs → systems → organism is the sequence of increasing complexity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following correctly shows increasing levels of organisation?
questions.explanation: Cells combine to form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together as systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Onion epidermis placed in strong sugar solution shows the cytoplasm shrunk away from the cell wall. The space between the cell wall and the shrunken protoplast is filled with
questions.explanation: The cell wall is fully permeable, so the external solution passes through it and surrounds the plasmolysed protoplast.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A drop of ink spreads faster in warm water than in cold water because at higher temperatures
questions.A: the water becomes less dense and floats the ink
questions.B: the ink dissolves the water more quickly
questions.C: the particles have more kinetic energy and move faster
questions.explanation: Diffusion depends on random particle motion, which increases with temperature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The cell membrane is described as selectively permeable because it
questions.A: allows all dissolved substances to pass through freely
questions.B: lets only water and nothing else through
questions.C: prevents every substance from entering the cell
questions.D: allows some substances to pass through but not others
questions.explanation: Small molecules like water and oxygen pass easily; large molecules and many ions are controlled by carrier proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Active transport differs from diffusion in that active transport
questions.A: moves substances only from a region of high to one of low concentration
questions.B: takes place only in dead cells whose membranes have broken down
questions.C: uses energy from respiration to move substances against a concentration gradient
questions.D: does not need the cell membrane or any energy from respiration
questions.explanation: Root hairs absorbing nitrate from dilute soil water and the gut absorbing glucose are examples; poisons that stop respiration stop active transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following organisms shows the cellular (unicellular) level of organisation?
questions.explanation: Paramecium is a single cell that carries out all life processes; Hydra has tissues, and the others have organs and systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The organelle that contains enzymes for digesting worn-out parts of the cell and engulfed bacteria is the
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound bags of hydrolytic enzymes; they also destroy the cell itself when it dies (autolysis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When onion cells are stained with iodine solution, a dark round body appears in each cell. This body is the
questions.explanation: Iodine stains the nucleus yellow-brown, making it stand out in the otherwise colourless onion epidermis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Plant cells placed in pure water swell but do not burst, whereas red blood cells do. This is because plant cells have
questions.A: a larger nucleus that resists the pressure of the water entering
questions.B: a much smaller amount of water in their cytoplasm than animal cells
questions.C: a strong cellulose cell wall that resists the pressure of water entering
questions.D: no cell membrane through which water could enter and burst them
questions.explanation: The rigid wall stops further water entry once the cell is turgid; an animal cell has only its thin membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The organelle responsible for the green colour of a leaf and the site of photosynthesis is the
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The correct path of a nerve impulse in a simple reflex arc is
questions.A: effector → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → receptor
questions.B: receptor → motor neurone → brain → sensory neurone → effector
questions.C: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
questions.D: sensory neurone → receptor → effector → motor neurone
questions.explanation: The impulse enters the spinal cord along the sensory neurone and leaves along the motor neurone to the muscle or gland.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a doctor taps the tendon just below a patient's kneecap, the lower leg jerks forward. The effector in this reflex is the
questions.explanation: Stretch receptors in the tendon fire, and the motor neurone makes the quadriceps contract, straightening the leg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person who has not eaten for several hours keeps a steady blood glucose level because
questions.A: insulin converts glycogen in the liver back to glucose
questions.B: adrenaline stops the muscles from using glucose
questions.C: glucagon causes the liver to convert stored glycogen to glucose
questions.D: the kidneys reabsorb extra glucose from the urine
questions.explanation: Glucagon from the pancreas raises blood glucose; insulin lowers it after a meal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An elderly man has to hold a newspaper at arm's length to read it. His defect is corrected with spectacles that have
questions.explanation: With age the lens loses its elasticity and cannot focus near objects (long sight); converging lenses add the missing power.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a torch is shone into a person's eye the pupil becomes smaller. This is brought about by
questions.C: contraction of the circular muscles of the iris
questions.explanation: The iris reflex protects the retina: circular muscles contract to narrow the pupil in bright light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the brain that controls memory, intelligence and voluntary actions is the
questions.explanation: The cerebrum, the largest part of the human brain, is the seat of conscious thought and voluntary movement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Hormonal coordination differs from nervous coordination in that hormonal responses are usually
questions.A: faster and last for a shorter time
questions.C: slower to start but last longer
questions.explanation: Hormones travel in the blood and act on many target organs for minutes to years; nerve impulses act in milliseconds on one effector.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person who has drunk a lot of alcohol staggers and speaks in a slurred way because alcohol
questions.A: stimulates the cerebrum to send more impulses
questions.B: makes the muscles swell and stiffen
questions.C: blocks the ears so that balance is lost
questions.D: depresses the nervous system, especially the cerebellum
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant; it slows impulses in the brain, impairing the cerebellum's control of balance and muscle coordination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A healthy child remains far shorter than other children of the same age. The most likely cause is under-secretion during childhood of
questions.C: growth hormone from the pituitary gland
questions.explanation: Growth hormone controls growth of bones and muscles; too little gives a pituitary dwarf, too much a giant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A patient passes very large volumes of dilute urine and is always thirsty, yet his blood glucose is normal. The hormone most likely lacking is
questions.explanation: ADH makes the kidney tubules reabsorb water; without it the tubules cannot concentrate the urine (diabetes insipidus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When the tip of a young oat seedling is cut off, the seedling no longer bends towards light from one side. This shows that
questions.A: the tip is the part that detects light and produces auxin
questions.B: the seedling needs its tip for photosynthesis
questions.C: cutting the tip kills the whole seedling
questions.D: the tip contains the cells that bend
questions.explanation: Auxin made at the tip moves to the shaded side and causes the cells below the tip to elongate; without the tip there is no auxin gradient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The tendrils of a passion-fruit vine coil round a stick they touch. This response is called
questions.explanation: Growth in response to touch (thigmotropism or haptotropism) allows climbing plants to grip supports.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The receptor cells for hearing are located in the
questions.explanation: Vibrations passed through the ossicles set up waves in the cochlear fluid, stimulating the sensory hair cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A boy cannot tell a red traffic light from a green one. The defective cells are the
questions.explanation: Cones are responsible for colour vision; an inherited defect in the red or green cones causes colour blindness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At the start of a 100 m race the sympathetic nervous system causes
questions.A: a slower heartbeat and constriction of the bronchioles
questions.B: constriction of the pupils and slower breathing
questions.C: increased flow of saliva and digestive juices
questions.D: a faster heartbeat and dilation of the bronchioles
questions.explanation: The sympathetic system prepares the body for action, working together with adrenaline.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A woman is thin and restless, has bulging eyes and a rapid heartbeat. These signs suggest
questions.explanation: Excess thyroxine raises the metabolic rate: weight loss, nervousness, fast pulse and protruding eyes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person cannot see an object whose image falls on the blind spot of the eye because at that point
questions.A: the lens cannot focus light onto that part of the retina
questions.B: the retina is covered by the iris and no light reaches it
questions.C: there are no rods or cones where the optic nerve leaves the eye
questions.D: the cornea is too thick for light to pass through to it
questions.explanation: The blind spot is where the nerve fibres gather to form the optic nerve, so it has no light-sensitive cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The gap between the end of one neurone and the beginning of the next, across which the impulse is passed by a chemical, is the
questions.explanation: Neurotransmitters released at the synapse diffuse across the gap and trigger an impulse in the next neurone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is an abiotic factor of a grassland habitat?
questions.B: the grasshoppers feeding on the grass
questions.C: the birds nesting in the trees
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are the non-living conditions: rainfall, temperature, light, wind and soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the food chain dead leaves → earthworm → bird → hawk, the chain begins with
questions.explanation: A chain that starts with dead material is a detritus food chain; the earthworm is a detritivore.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next. If the producers in a field store 10,000 kJ, the tertiary consumers receive about
questions.explanation: Producers 10,000 → primary 1,000 → secondary 100 → tertiary 10 kJ.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A woodpecker feeds on insects in tree bark while a hawk in the same forest hunts rodents. The two birds occupy the same habitat but different
questions.explanation: A niche is an organism's role in the ecosystem — what it eats, where it feeds and when.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cattle egrets follow grazing cattle and eat the insects disturbed by the cattle's feet; the cattle are unaffected. This relationship is
questions.explanation: One partner benefits and the other neither gains nor loses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mistletoe growing on a mango tree has green leaves but sends root-like structures into the branch to draw water and minerals. Mistletoe is
questions.explanation: It photosynthesises its own food but depends on the host for water and mineral salts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After a farmer killed all the snakes on his farm, the rat population rose sharply and destroyed his crops. This shows that the snakes were
questions.A: competitors of the rats for the same food
questions.B: decomposers that recycled nutrients on the farm
questions.C: parasites that fed on the blood of the rats
questions.D: predators that kept the rat population in check
questions.explanation: Removing a predator releases its prey from control — a common result of upsetting the balance of nature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The floor of a tropical rainforest has very little undergrowth because
questions.A: the dense canopy of tall trees lets very little light reach the ground
questions.B: the soil beneath the trees is too poor to support any small plants
questions.C: the many animals on the forest floor eat all the small plants
questions.D: the heavy rainfall washes away every seedling before it can grow
questions.explanation: Light is the limiting factor beneath the closed canopy; where a tree falls, a gap fills quickly with new growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Carbon(IV) oxide is returned to the atmosphere by all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis removes carbon(IV) oxide from the air; the other processes release it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Waterlogged soils lose fertility partly because denitrifying bacteria in them
questions.A: convert nitrates into nitrogen gas which escapes to the air
questions.C: fix nitrogen gas into the soil
questions.D: kill the earthworms that aerate the soil
questions.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria thrive where oxygen is scarce and break nitrates down to nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fish living in fast-flowing streams often have flattened bodies and sucker-like fins. These features help them to
questions.C: cling to rocks and avoid being swept away
questions.D: hide from predators in the mud
questions.explanation: Adaptations to a habitat match its physical conditions; here the main problem is the strong current.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 40 grasshoppers were caught in a field, marked and released. The next day 50 were caught, of which 10 were marked. The estimated population of grasshoppers in the field is
questions.explanation: Population = (first catch × second catch)/marked recaptured = 40 × 50/10 = 200.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a population of Paramecium in a culture reaches the carrying capacity of the dish, its growth slows down mainly because of
questions.A: competition for food and the build-up of wastes
questions.B: the increase in light reaching the dish
questions.C: the low temperature of the water
questions.explanation: Limited resources and accumulating toxic wastes raise the death rate until births and deaths balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The instrument used to measure wind speed in a habitat is the
questions.explanation: An anemometer's cups spin faster in stronger wind; a hygrometer measures humidity and a barometer air pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The water of a mangrove swamp near the coast is described as brackish because it
questions.A: is completely fresh, with no salt at all
questions.B: contains a lot of suspended mud
questions.C: is much saltier than the open sea
questions.D: is a mixture of fresh water and sea water
questions.explanation: Rivers meeting the sea produce water of intermediate salinity, which mangroves are adapted to tolerate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Plants of the Sahel savanna have small leaves, thick bark and very deep roots. These are adaptations to
questions.explanation: Small leaves cut water loss, thick bark protects from fire and heat, and deep roots reach ground water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A village had 2,000 people at the start of a year and 2,400 at the end. During the year 100 people died and nobody moved in or out. The number of births was
questions.explanation: Increase = births − deaths, so births = 400 + 100 = 500.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of organisms would compete most directly for food?
questions.A: a goat and a lion living in the same area
questions.B: a hawk and a mango tree in the same garden
questions.C: a cow and a goat grazing the same field
questions.D: a mosquito and a fish in the same pond
questions.explanation: Two herbivores eating the same grass in the same place compete for the same resource.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fossils found in the deepest layers of undisturbed sedimentary rock are generally
questions.C: the same age as those near the surface
questions.explanation: Sediments are laid down in order, so lower layers are older; the fossil record shows simpler forms first.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The wing of a bird and the wing of a butterfly perform the same function but have completely different structures. They are described as
questions.explanation: Analogous organs evolved separately for the same job (convergent evolution); homologous organs share a common origin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The early embryos of fish, birds and humans all show gill pouches and a tail. This similarity suggests that these animals
questions.A: all live in water at some stage
questions.B: will all develop gills as adults
questions.D: have the same number of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Comparative embryology is one of the lines of evidence for evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A farmer breeds only from the cows that give the most milk. Over many generations the milk yield of his herd rises. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Humans, not the environment, choose which individuals reproduce.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The sickle-cell gene remains common in West Africa although people with the SS genotype often die young. This is because people with the AS genotype
questions.A: are more resistant to malaria than AA people
questions.B: cannot pass the gene to their children
questions.D: produce more children than anyone else
questions.explanation: Heterozygote advantage: in malaria areas AS individuals survive better than both AA and SS, so the S allele is maintained.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: New alleles (new forms of genes) arise in a population by
questions.explanation: Mutations are the ultimate source of new genetic variation on which selection acts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fossils are most likely to form when an organism
questions.A: dies in the open where scavengers and bacteria break it down quickly
questions.B: is soft-bodied and decays quickly in warm, moist conditions
questions.C: is buried quickly in sediment and has hard parts such as bones or shells
questions.D: is burnt to ash in a bush fire and the ash is scattered by wind
questions.explanation: Rapid burial protects remains from decay and scavengers; minerals then replace the hard parts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: From one ancestral species, hundreds of species of cichlid fish with different feeding habits arose in Lake Victoria. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation is the rapid diversification of one lineage into many forms occupying different niches.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two populations of a lizard species were separated by a wide river for thousands of years. When brought together they can no longer interbreed. They have
questions.explanation: Geographical isolation prevents gene flow; the populations evolve separately until reproductive isolation makes them distinct species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Pythons have tiny claw-like remnants of hind limbs near the tail. This suggests that snakes
questions.A: are developing legs for the future
questions.B: use the claws to climb trees
questions.D: evolved from ancestors that had legs
questions.explanation: Vestigial structures are reduced remains of organs that were functional in ancestors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98% of their DNA. This is evidence that the two species
questions.A: descended from a common ancestor fairly recently
questions.explanation: The more similar the DNA and proteins of two species, the more recently they shared an ancestor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Darwin observed that organisms produce far more offspring than can survive. He concluded that
questions.A: most of the offspring are born dead or too weak to feed
questions.B: the environment always provides enough food and space for all
questions.C: there is a struggle for existence in which the best adapted survive
questions.D: all the offspring of a pair of parents are exactly alike
questions.explanation: Overproduction plus limited resources leads to competition; individuals with favourable variations survive and reproduce.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: DDT killed most mosquitoes when it was introduced in the 1950s but is now almost useless against them. This is because
questions.A: the mosquitoes learnt to avoid the sprayed areas and taught their young
questions.B: mosquitoes now breed only indoors where DDT cannot reach them
questions.C: DDT has slowly become weaker and less poisonous with age
questions.D: the few naturally resistant mosquitoes survived and passed on their resistance
questions.explanation: Insecticide resistance is natural selection observed within a human lifetime.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The idea that characteristics acquired during an organism's life, such as a blacksmith's strong arms, can be passed to its offspring was proposed by
questions.explanation: Lamarck's theory of the inheritance of acquired characters was later rejected because body changes do not alter the genes in gametes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A stick insect that closely resembles a twig is less likely to be eaten by birds. Over generations this resemblance became more perfect because
questions.A: the insects deliberately copied the twigs
questions.C: better-camouflaged insects survived and left more offspring
questions.explanation: Natural selection favours any heritable variation that improves survival.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The age of a fossil bone a few thousand years old is estimated by measuring the
questions.A: size of the bone compared with a modern one
questions.B: colour and hardness of the bone surface
questions.C: depth of the soil layer lying above it
questions.D: amount of radioactive carbon-14 remaining in it
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 decays at a known rate after death, so the proportion left gives the age (radiocarbon dating).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT evidence in support of evolution?
questions.B: similarities in the embryos of vertebrates
questions.C: the fact that all organisms need water
questions.D: vestigial organs such as the human appendix
questions.explanation: Needing water is a property of life itself, not evidence of descent with modification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Excess amino acids cannot be stored in the body. In the liver their amino groups are removed and converted to
questions.explanation: Deamination produces ammonia, which is quickly converted to the less poisonous urea and excreted by the kidneys.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sweat contains water, salts and a little urea. Besides excretion, sweating also
questions.A: warms the body on cold days
questions.C: cools the body as the water evaporates
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes latent heat from the skin, which is why sweating is greater in hot weather and during exercise.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney, in which urine is formed, is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, each with a glomerulus, capsule, tubule and loop of Henle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following substances is NOT normally found in the fluid filtered into the Bowman's capsule?
questions.explanation: Proteins and blood cells are too large to pass through the walls of the glomerular capillaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Glucose, amino acids and most of the water are reabsorbed from the filtrate in the
questions.explanation: The first coiled part of the tubule, lined with cells rich in mitochondria and microvilli, reabsorbs useful substances.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A patient whose kidneys have failed is kept alive by a dialysis machine. The machine works by
questions.A: pumping fresh blood into the patient every week
questions.B: filtering the patient's urine and returning it to the body
questions.C: removing urea and excess salts from the blood through a partially permeable membrane
questions.D: adding oxygen to the blood under pressure
questions.explanation: Blood flows past dialysis fluid separated by a membrane; wastes diffuse out while blood cells and proteins are kept.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The yellow colour of urine is due mainly to
questions.A: the large amount of dissolved urea in it
questions.B: dissolved salts such as sodium chloride
questions.C: excess glucose that the body cannot use
questions.D: pigments formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Bile pigments from worn-out red cells are excreted in bile and, after modification, in urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Insects and birds excrete their nitrogenous waste as uric acid, a solid, rather than as urea. This is an advantage because it
questions.explanation: Uric acid is almost insoluble and can be passed as a paste with very little water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Freshwater fish produce large volumes of very dilute urine because
questions.A: water constantly enters their bodies by osmosis
questions.B: they drink a lot of water
questions.explanation: The body fluids are more concentrated than fresh water, so water flows in through the gills and must be pumped out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The contractile vacuole of Amoeba functions to
questions.C: remove excess water from the cell
questions.explanation: Water entering by osmosis collects in the vacuole, which swells and then bursts to the outside.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Tannins, gums and resins found in the bark and heartwood of trees are
questions.A: foods stored for the dry season
questions.D: waste products stored in dead tissues
questions.explanation: Plants have no special excretory organs; many wastes are deposited in tissues that are later shed or are already dead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After drinking several bottles of beer a man passes a large amount of urine. This is because alcohol
questions.A: reduces the release of ADH so less water is reabsorbed
questions.B: increases the amount of ADH released
questions.explanation: Less antidiuretic hormone means the collecting ducts stay impermeable to water and dilute urine is produced.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The correct sequence through which filtrate passes in a nephron is
questions.A: Bowman's capsule → loop of Henle → proximal tubule → collecting duct
questions.B: proximal tubule → Bowman's capsule → distal tubule → loop of Henle
questions.C: Bowman's capsule → proximal tubule → loop of Henle → distal tubule → collecting duct
questions.D: collecting duct → distal tubule → loop of Henle → Bowman's capsule
questions.explanation: Filtrate leaves the capsule, passes the proximal tubule, the loop, the distal tubule and finally the collecting duct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The liver is regarded as an excretory organ because it
questions.explanation: Urea from deamination and bilirubin from haemoglobin breakdown are both made in the liver.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of
questions.explanation: They lie in the blood-filled body cavity of insects and empty uric acid into the hind gut.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The excretory structures of the flatworm Planaria are
questions.explanation: Flame cells with beating cilia drive water and wastes along tubules to pores on the body surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The kidney helps to keep the pH of the blood constant by
questions.A: excreting excess hydrogen ions in the urine
questions.C: removing all the salts from the blood
questions.explanation: Kidney tubule cells secrete H⁺ into the filtrate and reabsorb hydrogencarbonate, so urine is usually slightly acidic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A dry bean seed soaked in water overnight almost doubles in size. This increase is NOT regarded as true growth because
questions.A: it is caused only by uptake of water and can be reversed by drying
questions.B: the seed does not need light to increase in size in this way
questions.C: the seed coat has not been broken by the swelling of the seed
questions.D: no oxygen is used while the seed is soaking in the water
questions.explanation: Growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass; imbibition of water is reversible.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The region of a root tip where cells are actively dividing by mitosis is
questions.A: the root cap at the very tip of the root
questions.B: the region of elongation behind the tip
questions.C: the region of root hairs behind the tip
questions.D: the meristematic region just behind the root cap
questions.explanation: The root cap protects the delicate meristem, whose new cells then enlarge in the region of elongation and mature further back.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The increase in height of a maize plant results from the activity of the
questions.A: apical meristem at the shoot tip
questions.C: root hairs on the young roots
questions.explanation: Apical meristems at shoot and root tips produce primary growth in length.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A graph of the height of a seedling against time is S-shaped (sigmoid). The steepest part of the curve represents the period when
questions.explanation: The slope of a growth curve is the growth rate; the curve later flattens as the plant matures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell with 20 chromosomes divides by mitosis. Each daughter cell will have
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells with the same chromosome number as the parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A young grasshopper looks like a small adult but has no wings; it develops wings gradually as it moults. This type of development is
questions.explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis has three stages — egg, nymph, adult — with no pupa; butterflies and houseflies show complete metamorphosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Maize grains stored in a dry barn for two years still germinate when planted. During storage the grains were
questions.A: dormant, with a very low rate of metabolism
questions.B: dead, with no metabolism taking place
questions.C: growing very slowly in the dry barn
questions.explanation: Dormant seeds respire slowly and remain alive until water, warmth and oxygen trigger germination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The first structure to emerge from a germinating maize grain is the
questions.explanation: The radicle grows out first to anchor the seedling and absorb water; the plumule follows.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bean seedlings grown in a dark cupboard are tall, thin and yellow with small leaves. This condition is called
questions.explanation: Without light, chlorophyll is not made and the stem elongates rapidly as the seedling 'searches' for light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Some plants flower only when the days become short at the end of the rainy season. This response to the length of day is called
questions.explanation: Photoperiodism controls flowering, leaf fall and dormancy in many plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Dwarf pea plants sprayed with a plant hormone grew as tall as normal varieties. The hormone was most likely
questions.explanation: Gibberellins stimulate stem elongation; genetic dwarfs often lack them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After cells produced by a meristem have enlarged, they take up particular shapes and functions, such as xylem vessels or guard cells. This process is called
questions.explanation: Differentiation converts identical new cells into the specialised cells of tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT normally required for the germination of most seeds?
questions.explanation: Most seeds germinate as well in darkness as in light; water, oxygen and warmth are essential.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A maize plant was 12 cm tall when first measured and 60 cm tall six weeks later. Its average growth rate over the period was
questions.explanation: (60 − 12)/6 = 8 cm per week.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The change of a tadpole into a frog, involving loss of the tail and growth of legs, is an example of
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is a marked change of form during development, controlled in amphibians by thyroxine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is the best evidence that growth has taken place in a plant?
questions.A: an increase in fresh mass after watering
questions.B: the drooping of its leaves at midday
questions.C: the opening of its flowers in the morning
questions.D: a permanent increase in dry mass
questions.explanation: Dry mass excludes the water content, which changes from hour to hour, and so reflects real production of new material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Human skin cells and gut lining cells are replaced continuously throughout life by
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces identical cells for growth and for the replacement of worn-out cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The hereditary material that carries information from parents to offspring is
questions.explanation: Genes are lengths of DNA on the chromosomes in the nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two maize plants with exactly the same genotype were grown, one in fertile soil and the other in poor soil. The plant in poor soil was much shorter. This shows that
questions.A: the genotype of a plant changes with the soil
questions.C: height in maize is not inherited
questions.D: the phenotype depends on both genotype and environment
questions.explanation: The genes set the potential; the environment determines how much of it is expressed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An albino child is born to two normally pigmented parents. The parents must both be
questions.A: heterozygous carriers of the albino allele
questions.explanation: Albinism is recessive; a child can be aa only if each parent contributed an a allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Both parents are carriers of the recessive allele for albinism (Aa). The probability that their next child will be an albino is
questions.explanation: Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, Aa, aa — one in four, or 25%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A couple already have three daughters. The probability that their fourth child will be a boy is
questions.explanation: Each fertilisation is independent; half of the father's sperm carry Y, so the chance of a boy is always 1/2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A Rhesus-negative woman may have complications when carrying her second Rhesus-positive baby because
questions.A: her anti-Rhesus antibodies, made after the first birth, cross the placenta and destroy the baby's red cells
questions.B: the second baby always has a different Rhesus group from the first and reacts against the mother
questions.C: her blood changes to Rhesus-positive after the first pregnancy and clots in the second baby
questions.D: the second baby inherits antibodies from the father which attack the mother's red blood cells
questions.explanation: Sensitisation usually happens at the first birth; in later pregnancies the anti-Rhesus antibodies attack the fetus (haemolytic disease of the newborn).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person of blood group AB has both A and B antigens on the red cells. The alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ are therefore described as
questions.explanation: Neither allele masks the other; both are fully expressed in the heterozygote.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The ABO blood group system is controlled by
questions.explanation: Iᴬ, Iᴮ and Iᴼ are multiple alleles; each person carries two of the three.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A maize plant heterozygous for two independent characters (AaBb) is test-crossed with a plant of genotype aabb. The expected phenotypic ratio among the offspring is
questions.explanation: The aabb parent gives only ab gametes, so the four gamete types of the AaBb parent (AB, Ab, aB, ab) each produce a different phenotype in equal numbers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The number of different kinds of gamete produced by a plant of genotype AaBb (genes on different chromosomes) is
questions.explanation: Independent assortment gives AB, Ab, aB and ab.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of physiological variation in humans?
questions.B: skin colour from light to dark
questions.D: shape and size of the nose and ears
questions.explanation: Physiological variations concern how the body functions (tasting PTC, blood group); height and skin colour are morphological.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A farmer crosses a high-yielding maize variety with a disease-resistant one and selects offspring that show both qualities. This method of improving crops is called
questions.explanation: Cross-breeding combines desirable genes from two varieties; selection keeps the best combinations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man of genotype AS marries a woman of genotype SS. The percentage of their children expected to have sickle-cell anaemia is
questions.explanation: AS × SS gives AS and SS in equal numbers, so half the children are expected to be SS.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fraternal (non-identical) twins are genetically different because they develop from
questions.A: two different ova fertilised by two different sperm
questions.B: one ovum fertilised by one sperm that later split
questions.C: one ovum fertilised by two sperm
questions.D: two ova fertilised by the same sperm
questions.explanation: Fraternal twins are no more alike than ordinary brothers and sisters and may be of different sexes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Exposure to X-rays, ultraviolet light and certain chemicals such as mustard gas can cause
questions.explanation: These mutagens damage DNA; mutations in gametes are passed to offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Children of the same parents differ from one another mainly because of
questions.A: differences in the food they eat while they are growing up
questions.B: mutations caused by sunlight falling on their skin
questions.C: crossing over, independent assortment and random fertilisation
questions.D: differences in their order of birth and in their upbringing
questions.explanation: Meiosis shuffles the alleles into countless gamete combinations, and any sperm may fertilise any egg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Down's syndrome results when a child has one extra chromosome, giving a total of
questions.explanation: Normal human cells have 46 chromosomes; non-disjunction of chromosome 21 gives 47.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Refuse dumped in open gutters in a city blocks the drains and, apart from causing floods, it also
questions.A: improves the fertility of the soil nearby
questions.C: purifies the water flowing in the gutters
questions.D: provides breeding places for mosquitoes, flies and rats
questions.explanation: Stagnant water breeds mosquitoes; decaying refuse attracts flies and rats that spread disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: To conserve the fish stock of a river, the government should
questions.A: ban the use of nets with very small mesh and impose a closed season
questions.B: encourage fishing all year round with any net
questions.C: add fertiliser to the river to feed the fish
questions.D: drain the river every dry season
questions.explanation: Small-mesh nets remove young fish before they breed; a closed season lets the fish spawn.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Yearly bush burning to clear farmland is harmful mainly because it
questions.A: destroys humus and kills useful soil organisms, leaving the soil bare to erosion
questions.B: makes the soil too wet and waterlogged for most crops to grow
questions.C: adds too much nitrogen to the soil and scorches the young crops
questions.D: increases the number of earthworms so much that they eat the roots
questions.explanation: Fire burns off organic matter, kills micro-organisms and removes the vegetation cover that protects the soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vaccinating a child against measles protects the child because the vaccine
questions.A: stimulates the body to produce its own antibodies and memory cells
questions.B: kills any measles virus already in the body
questions.C: supplies ready-made antibodies from another person
questions.D: blocks the virus from entering the body
questions.explanation: Active immunity develops when a harmless form of the pathogen triggers the immune system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Typhoid fever is spread mainly through
questions.A: the bite of an infected mosquito
questions.B: droplets breathed out by an infected person
questions.C: food and water contaminated with faeces of an infected person
questions.D: contact with the skin of a patient
questions.explanation: Salmonella typhi is a water- and food-borne bacterium; clean water and good sanitation prevent it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Tuberculosis spreads from one person to another mainly through
questions.A: droplets coughed or sneezed into the air
questions.C: the bite of the tsetse fly
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is carried in airborne droplets, which is why overcrowded housing favours its spread.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, is NOT transmitted by
questions.A: unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
questions.B: sharing needles or razor blades with an infected person
questions.C: sharing cups and plates with an infected person
questions.D: transfusion of blood taken from an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is carried in blood, semen, vaginal fluid and breast milk, not in saliva on utensils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The stage of the malaria parasite injected into a person by a feeding female Anopheles mosquito is the
questions.explanation: Sporozoites from the mosquito's salivary glands travel to the liver and later invade red blood cells as merozoites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The Cross River gorilla is protected in Nigeria mainly by
questions.A: setting aside national parks and banning hunting
questions.C: feeding the gorillas with farm crops
questions.D: clearing the forest to see them better
questions.explanation: Conservation of wildlife depends on protecting the habitat and preventing poaching.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The deep gullies found in parts of south-eastern Nigeria were caused mainly by
questions.A: earthquakes that split the ground open in the wet season
questions.B: the burrowing of large numbers of soil animals over many years
questions.C: running water eroding soil from which vegetation had been removed
questions.D: the excessive use of chemical fertilisers on farms in the area
questions.explanation: Without plant roots to bind it, loose soil on slopes is carried away by heavy rain, forming gullies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Large-scale felling of forest trees without replanting leads to all of the following EXCEPT
questions.A: loss of habitat for wild animals
questions.C: an increase in the oxygen content of the air
questions.D: a rise in carbon(IV) oxide in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Fewer trees means less photosynthesis, so oxygen release falls and carbon(IV) oxide is no longer removed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Living next to a generator that runs all night can eventually cause
questions.explanation: Prolonged loud noise damages the sensory hair cells of the cochlea; noise is a form of pollution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fish die in large numbers after an oil spill in a river mainly because the oil
questions.A: makes the water far too salty for freshwater fish to survive in
questions.B: provides so much food that the fish overeat and die
questions.C: makes the water too cold for the fish to keep swimming
questions.D: forms a film that stops oxygen dissolving and coats the gills of the fish
questions.explanation: The oil layer cuts off gas exchange at the surface, and toxic components poison aquatic life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Introducing a natural predator to reduce the population of a crop pest is an example of
questions.explanation: Biological control avoids the pollution and resistance problems of pesticides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The population of a country grows fastest when its
questions.A: birth rate is much higher than its death rate
questions.B: death rate is higher than its birth rate
questions.C: birth rate and death rate are equal
questions.explanation: Population change = births − deaths (+ net migration).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A pit latrine should be sited at least 30 metres away from, and downhill of, a well in order to
questions.A: keep the water in the well cool during the dry season
questions.B: make the latrine easier for the whole village to reach
questions.C: prevent faecal organisms from seeping into the drinking water
questions.D: stop mosquitoes from breeding in the water of the well
questions.explanation: Organisms causing cholera, typhoid and dysentery travel through soil water into badly sited wells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The vector of onchocerciasis (river blindness) is the
questions.explanation: Simulium breeds in fast-flowing rivers and transmits the worm Onchocerca volvulus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The transmission of cholera in a community is best prevented by
questions.A: providing safe drinking water and proper disposal of sewage
questions.B: sleeping under insecticide-treated nets every night
questions.C: spraying the walls of houses with insecticide
questions.D: vaccinating all the dogs and cats in the community
questions.explanation: Cholera is spread by water and food contaminated with the faeces of infected people.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following meals is best balanced?
questions.B: bread and a bottle of soft drink
questions.C: rice, beans, vegetables, fish and an orange
questions.explanation: A balanced meal supplies carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamins, minerals, roughage and water in the right proportions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A child who cannot see well in dim light but sees normally by day is most likely short of
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed to make the pigment in the rods; its deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A pregnant woman is advised to take extra milk and fish in her diet mainly because the developing baby needs
questions.A: calcium for its bones and teeth
questions.explanation: Calcium (and vitamin D) are needed for bone and tooth formation; the baby draws on the mother's supply.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The digestion of protein begins in the
questions.explanation: Pepsin, secreted by the stomach wall, works in the acidic gastric juice to break proteins into peptides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Three tubes containing starch solution and amylase were kept at 0 °C, 37 °C and 60 °C. Starch disappeared fastest in the tube at 37 °C because
questions.A: the enzyme works best at its optimum temperature
questions.B: starch dissolves most quickly in water at 37 °C
questions.C: amylase is destroyed by the cold at 0 °C
questions.D: water boils at 37 °C and breaks down the starch
questions.explanation: Below the optimum the enzyme works slowly; at 60 °C it is denatured and stops working.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bubbles of gas collected from a water plant in bright sunlight relight a glowing splint. The gas is
questions.explanation: Oxygen is released from the splitting of water during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.explanation: In the light reaction water is split (photolysis) into hydrogen, used to reduce CO₂, and oxygen, which is given off.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: On a bright, warm day the rate of photosynthesis of a well-watered plant is most likely limited by
questions.A: the concentration of carbon(IV) oxide in the air
questions.B: the intensity of the light falling on the leaves
questions.C: the amount of water available in the soil
questions.D: the amount of chlorophyll in the leaves
questions.explanation: With plenty of light and warmth, the 0.04% carbon(IV) oxide in air becomes the factor in shortest supply.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following organisms is an autotroph?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a green alga that makes its own food by photosynthesis; the others feed on ready-made organic matter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The correct sequence of processes in holozoic nutrition is
questions.explanation: Food is taken in, broken down, absorbed, built into the body, and the undigested remains are passed out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Digested fats (fatty acids and glycerol) are absorbed mainly into the
questions.A: lacteals of the villi in the ileum
questions.explanation: Fat products enter the lymph vessels (lacteals) of the villi and reach the blood later; sugars and amino acids enter the capillaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A dog has large, pointed teeth at the corners of its jaws. These teeth are used for
questions.explanation: Canines are well developed in carnivores for seizing and tearing prey.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cattle can live on grass alone because the bacteria in their rumen
questions.B: kill the parasites in the grass
questions.explanation: Mammals do not make cellulase; the symbiotic micro-organisms ferment cellulose into fatty acids the cow can absorb.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After a meal, the excess glucose absorbed into the blood is converted in the liver to
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes the storage of glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Vegetables and fruits should be included in the diet partly because they supply roughage, which
questions.A: adds bulk to the food and helps to prevent constipation
questions.B: provides most of the energy that the body needs each day
questions.C: builds up the muscles and repairs worn-out tissues
questions.D: is digested slowly into the vitamins the body needs
questions.explanation: Cellulose fibre is not digested but stimulates peristalsis in the gut.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A plant grown in a culture solution lacking phosphorus shows poor root development and stunted growth because phosphorus is needed for
questions.explanation: Phosphate is part of ATP, DNA and RNA and of cell membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Dodder (Cuscuta), a yellow thread-like plant with no chlorophyll, twines round hedges and obtains its food by
questions.B: absorbing decaying matter from the soil
questions.D: sending suckers (haustoria) into the host plant's tissues
questions.explanation: Dodder is a total parasite; its haustoria tap the host's phloem and xylem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mushrooms growing on a rotting log obtain their food by
questions.A: secreting enzymes onto the wood and absorbing the digested products
questions.B: photosynthesis using the little light that reaches the log
questions.C: trapping and digesting the small insects that land on them
questions.D: sucking sap from the living trees growing near the log
questions.explanation: Saprophytic nutrition: extracellular digestion of dead organic matter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Amoeba reproduces asexually by
questions.explanation: The nucleus divides by mitosis and the cell then splits into two equal daughter cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bread mould (Rhizopus) spreads rapidly over a piece of bread by producing large numbers of
questions.explanation: The black dots on mouldy bread are sporangia; each releases thousands of light spores carried by air.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Cassava is usually propagated by farmers using
questions.explanation: Pieces of mature stem with several nodes root easily and produce plants identical to the parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An advantage of propagating a good variety of plantain by suckers rather than by seeds is that the new plants
questions.A: show a great deal of useful variation from the parent
questions.B: can be dispersed over long distances by wind and animals
questions.C: are genetically identical to the parent and mature quickly
questions.D: are resistant to all the diseases that attack plantain
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation preserves desirable qualities exactly, but the crop is uniform and equally vulnerable to any new disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The lining of the uterus breaks down and is shed during menstruation because
questions.A: the ovum has not been fertilised and progesterone level falls
questions.B: too much oestrogen is produced by the ovaries at that time
questions.C: the ovum has been fertilised and the embryo needs the blood
questions.D: the placenta has stopped working at the end of the month
questions.explanation: Without a pregnancy the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and the thickened lining is lost.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Menstruation stops during pregnancy because
questions.A: the ovaries are removed from the body during pregnancy
questions.B: the pituitary gland stops working until the baby is born
questions.C: the uterus becomes too small to shed any of its lining
questions.D: high levels of progesterone maintain the lining of the uterus
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum and later the placenta keep producing progesterone, which prevents shedding of the lining and further ovulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The middle piece of a sperm cell contains many mitochondria in order to
questions.A: supply energy for the beating of the tail
questions.B: carry the genetic material to the ovum
questions.C: penetrate the outer membrane of the ovum
questions.D: protect the sperm from the acid in the vagina
questions.explanation: Swimming to the ovum needs a great deal of ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The umbilical vein of a fetus carries
questions.A: deoxygenated blood and wastes to the placenta
questions.B: urine from the fetus to the mother
questions.C: oxygenated blood and nutrients from the placenta to the fetus
questions.D: the mother's blood into the fetus
questions.explanation: Exchange takes place across the placenta; maternal and fetal blood never mix.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In some flowers the anthers ripen and shed their pollen before the stigma of the same flower is ready to receive it. This
questions.B: prevents pollination of the flower altogether
questions.C: ensures self-pollination within the same flower
questions.D: attracts more insects to the flower at the right time
questions.explanation: Protandry is one of several devices (with self-sterility and separate sexes) that favour cross-pollination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After pollination the pollen tube grows down through the style and enters the ovule through the
questions.explanation: The male gametes travel down the tube and are released near the embryo sac inside the ovule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tomato, with many seeds embedded in juicy flesh, is classified as a
questions.explanation: A berry is a fleshy fruit with several seeds and no stony layer; a mango (one stone) is a drupe.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A fruit differs from a seed in that a fruit develops from the
questions.explanation: After fertilisation the ovary wall becomes the fruit wall and each ovule becomes a seed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The dry pods of the pride of Barbados (Caesalpinia) twist and split open suddenly on a hot afternoon, scattering the seeds. This method of dispersal is called
questions.explanation: Unequal drying of the pod wall builds up tension that is released explosively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The coconut fruit is adapted for dispersal by water because it has
questions.A: a fibrous husk that traps air and makes it float
questions.B: a very heavy stony seed that sinks to the sea bed
questions.C: hooks on its surface that catch on passing animals
questions.D: bright red flesh that attracts birds and monkeys
questions.explanation: Coconuts drift for weeks and germinate on distant shores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Rabbits give birth to fully formed young while hens lay eggs. Rabbits are described as
questions.explanation: Viviparous animals nourish the embryo inside the mother and give birth to live young.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The earthworm has both male and female organs, yet two worms must mate to reproduce. This is because
questions.A: its sperm and eggs ripen at different times, so it must cross-fertilise
questions.B: each worm has only one working sex organ and needs the other's
questions.C: its eggs cannot develop unless two worms make the cocoon together
questions.D: the two worms need to exchange food before either can lay eggs
questions.explanation: Hermaphrodites usually exchange sperm; cross-fertilisation increases variation among the offspring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pollen grains, which produce the male gametes of a flowering plant, are formed in the
questions.explanation: The anther is the fertile part of the stamen; the filament merely holds it up.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tadpole hatches from a toad's egg laid in a pond. At this stage it breathes with
questions.explanation: The aquatic larva has external, then internal gills; lungs develop during metamorphosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The word equation for aerobic respiration is
questions.A: carbon(IV) oxide + water → glucose + oxygen + energy
questions.C: glucose + oxygen → carbon(IV) oxide + water + energy
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration completely oxidises glucose, releasing about 2,900 kJ per mole.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The stage of respiration that produces the largest amount of ATP takes place in the
questions.explanation: Glycolysis in the cytoplasm yields only 2 ATP; the Krebs cycle and electron transport chain in the mitochondria yield the rest.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Glycolysis, the first stage of respiration, takes place in the cytoplasm and converts one molecule of glucose into
questions.explanation: Glucose (6 carbons) is split into two 3-carbon pyruvate molecules with a small net gain of ATP; oxygen is not needed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The products of anaerobic respiration in yeast and in human muscle are respectively
questions.A: ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide; lactic acid
questions.B: lactic acid; ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide
questions.C: carbon(IV) oxide and water; lactic acid
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar to alcohol and CO₂; muscles form lactic acid, which is later oxidised when oxygen is available.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fresh palm wine tapped in the morning froths and tastes alcoholic by evening because
questions.A: the sugar in it evaporates in the heat
questions.B: oxygen from the air turns the sugar to alcohol
questions.C: wild yeasts ferment its sugars anaerobically
questions.D: the palm tree adds alcohol to the sap
questions.explanation: Yeasts convert the sugars in the sap to ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide, which produces the froth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The alveoli of the lungs are efficient surfaces for gas exchange because they
questions.A: are thick-walled and dry, so that dust cannot pass through them
questions.B: are lined with cilia that absorb oxygen directly from the air
questions.C: contain strong muscles that pump the air in and out of the lungs
questions.D: are thin-walled, moist, very numerous and surrounded by capillaries
questions.explanation: Millions of alveoli give a surface of about 70 m², separated from the blood by two thin cell layers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Tar in cigarette smoke destroys the cilia lining the air passages. As a result, smokers
questions.A: cannot clear mucus and dust from the lungs and develop a persistent cough
questions.B: breathe more deeply than non-smokers to make up for the lost cilia
questions.C: produce far more red blood cells to carry the extra oxygen
questions.D: take in more oxygen with each breath because the airways are wider
questions.explanation: The cilia normally sweep mucus and trapped particles up to the throat; without them the lungs become congested.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: People sleeping in a closed room with a running petrol generator can die because carbon(II) oxide
questions.A: makes the air in the room too hot and dry for the lungs to breathe
questions.B: dissolves the thin walls of the alveoli so that the lungs collapse
questions.C: combines with haemoglobin more firmly than oxygen does, so the blood carries no oxygen
questions.D: causes the lungs to fill with water so that the sleepers drown
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is very stable; the tissues are starved of oxygen even though breathing continues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Gas exchange in the leaves of a plant takes place mainly through the
questions.explanation: Stomata (mainly on the lower surface) open by day; woody stems use lenticels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The energy released during respiration is stored in the cell in the form of
questions.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate is the immediate energy currency used for muscle contraction, active transport and synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At night a green plant
questions.A: takes in carbon(IV) oxide and gives out oxygen
questions.B: neither takes in nor gives out any gas
questions.C: takes in oxygen and gives out carbon(IV) oxide
questions.D: gives out both oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis stops in the dark but respiration continues all the time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At dawn there comes a moment when a leaf shows no net uptake or release of carbon(IV) oxide. At this point
questions.A: photosynthesis has not yet started because the light is too dim
questions.B: the stomata are closed, so no gas can enter or leave the leaf
questions.C: respiration has stopped because the leaf has used up its sugar
questions.D: the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration
questions.explanation: This is the compensation point; above it the plant gains sugar, below it the plant uses its reserves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A frog can exchange gases through all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Adult frogs lose the gills of the tadpole; the skin is important especially when the frog is under water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An earthworm dies if its skin dries out because
questions.A: oxygen must dissolve in the moist skin before it can diffuse into the blood
questions.B: it can no longer move through the soil to look for food
questions.C: it loses all the food stored in the cells of its skin
questions.D: the dry skin cracks and lets in parasites and bacteria
questions.explanation: Gas exchange in earthworms takes place only across a moist, thin, well-vascularised skin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Breathing differs from respiration in that breathing is
questions.A: the release of energy from food in the cells
questions.B: the mechanical movement of air into and out of the lungs
questions.C: the transport of oxygen by the blood
questions.D: the production of carbon(IV) oxide by cells
questions.explanation: Breathing (ventilation) merely supplies the gas exchange surface; respiration is the chemical process inside cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A footballer from Lagos tires very quickly when playing a match in a city 3,000 m above sea level because
questions.A: the air there is too hot
questions.B: each breath of the thin air contains less oxygen
questions.C: there is too much carbon(IV) oxide in the air
questions.explanation: The lower air pressure means less oxygen diffuses into the blood; visitors adapt slowly by making more red blood cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a respirometer containing soda lime and a live cockroach, the coloured liquid in the capillary tube moves towards the animal because
questions.A: the animal pushes the liquid along the tube with its legs and antennae
questions.B: oxygen is used up and the carbon(IV) oxide produced is absorbed by the soda lime
questions.C: the animal breathes out warm air that draws the liquid towards it
questions.D: the soda lime gives off a gas that pulls the liquid along the tube
questions.explanation: The fall in volume inside the tube measures the rate of oxygen consumption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Soil is formed from rocks mainly by the process of
questions.explanation: Weathering by heat, water, ice, wind and living things breaks rocks into the mineral particles of soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The layer of a soil profile that is richest in humus and living organisms is the
questions.explanation: Dead leaves and roots decay in the topsoil, giving it a dark colour and most of the soil life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ploughing or hoeing a field before planting improves the soil mainly by
questions.A: adding nitrogen compounds to the soil from the air
questions.B: breaking up clods and letting air and water into it
questions.C: killing all the earthworms and insects in the soil
questions.D: removing the topsoil so that the subsoil is exposed
questions.explanation: Loosened soil is better aerated and drained and allows roots to penetrate easily.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 100 cm³ of water was poured onto 100 g of dry clay soil in a funnel and 40 cm³ drained through. The volume of water retained by the soil was
questions.explanation: Water retained = water added − water drained = 100 − 40 = 60 cm³.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A 50 g sample of fresh garden soil was dried in an oven until its mass stayed constant at 40 g. The percentage of water in the soil was

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A sample of dry soil was heated strongly in a crucible until it turned grey and lost mass. The loss of mass represents the
questions.explanation: Organic matter burns away on strong heating, leaving the mineral ash.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A farmer adds lime (calcium hydroxide) to his field because the soil is too acidic. The lime
questions.explanation: Lime neutralises soil acids; most crops grow best at pH 6–7.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bacteria and fungi in the soil help plants mainly by
questions.A: eating the pests and worms that attack the roots of the plants
questions.B: decomposing dead matter and releasing mineral salts that plants absorb
questions.C: shading the surface of the soil from the heat of the sun
questions.D: producing the oxygen that the roots need for respiration
questions.explanation: Decomposers recycle nitrogen, phosphorus and other nutrients locked up in dead organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Covering the soil around crops with a layer of dry grass (mulching) helps mainly by
questions.A: attracting more insects and birds to the farm to pollinate the crops
questions.B: reducing evaporation and erosion while adding humus as it rots
questions.C: making the soil more acidic so that weeds cannot grow in it
questions.D: stopping the roots from breathing so that they grow deeper
questions.explanation: Mulch keeps the soil moist and cool, suppresses weeds and eventually decays into humus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A field cropped with maize every year without fertiliser gives smaller and smaller yields because
questions.A: the soil becomes too loose for the roots to anchor the plants
questions.B: the mineral nutrients removed in the harvest are not replaced
questions.C: the maize plants release poisons that build up in the soil
questions.D: the temperature of the soil rises a little more each year
questions.explanation: Each crop takes nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium out of the soil; fallowing, rotation or fertilisers restore them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A soil sample shaken with water in a measuring cylinder and left to settle forms layers. The layer at the bottom consists of
questions.explanation: The heaviest and largest particles settle first; humus floats on the surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The soil particles arranged in order of decreasing size are
questions.explanation: Gravel > 2 mm, sand 0.02–2 mm, silt 0.002–0.02 mm, clay < 0.002 mm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Allowing too many cattle to graze a piece of land for a long time leads to
questions.B: bare soil that is easily eroded
questions.explanation: Overgrazing strips the protective vegetation and compacts the soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ploughing a growing crop of young cowpea plants into the soil to add organic matter is called
questions.explanation: The buried plants decay into humus and, being legumes, add nitrogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The letters N, P and K on a bag of fertiliser stand for
questions.explanation: These are the three macronutrients that crops remove from the soil in the largest amounts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Clay soil is described as heavy and poorly drained because its particles
questions.A: are large and rounded with big air spaces between them
questions.B: are very small and pack closely, leaving tiny pores
questions.C: contain a lot of humus that soaks up all the water
questions.D: are made of coarse gravel that holds water on its surface
questions.explanation: Tiny pores hold water by capillarity and let very little drain through or air enter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following statements about earthworms in the soil is correct?
questions.A: they eat the roots of crops and reduce yields
questions.B: their burrows aerate the soil and their casts enrich it
questions.C: they make the soil too acidic for crops
questions.D: they spread plant diseases from farm to farm
questions.explanation: Earthworms mix and aerate the soil and their casts are rich in available nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Besides supporting the body, the long bones of the limbs also
questions.A: produce the hormones that control growth
questions.B: manufacture blood cells in their marrow
questions.C: store urine until it is passed out
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The skeleton of a cockroach is
questions.explanation: Arthropods have a hard outer cuticle of chitin to which the muscles are attached from inside.

questions.subject: Biology
