questions.q: The vertebrae with the largest, strongest centra, found in the lower back, are the
questions.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae bear most of the weight of the upper body and have large centra and processes for the back muscles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The discs of cartilage found between the vertebrae serve to
questions.A: join the ribs firmly to the spine at the back
questions.B: absorb shock and allow slight movement between vertebrae
questions.C: produce the red blood cells needed by the body
questions.D: protect the brain from injury during a fall
questions.explanation: Intervertebral discs cushion the spine during running and jumping.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A footballer twists his knee and tears the tough tissue that joins the thigh bone to the shin bone. The damaged tissue is a
questions.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone at joints; tendons join muscle to bone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The joints between the bones of the skull are
questions.explanation: The skull bones are locked together by sutures that allow no movement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The fluid found in the capsule of a movable joint such as the knee serves to
questions.B: lubricate the joint and reduce friction
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid is secreted by the synovial membrane lining the joint capsule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The muscle that contracts rhythmically throughout life without becoming tired is
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, has its own rhythm and is richly supplied with mitochondria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Trees remain upright even in the dry season when their cells are short of water because they are supported mainly by
questions.C: the pressure of sap in the phloem
questions.explanation: Woody tissues provide rigid mechanical support independent of turgor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The strings that can be pulled from a stalk of celery or the midrib of a leaf are strands of flexible supporting tissue called
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells have thickened corners and support young, growing parts without stopping them bending.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The deep keel on the breastbone of a bird serves for the
questions.A: storage of fat for long flights
questions.B: attachment of the large flight muscles
questions.explanation: The pectoral muscles that pull the wings down are anchored to the keel.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A bony fish is able to stay at any depth without swimming because of its
questions.explanation: Adjusting the gas in the swim bladder changes the fish's density to match the water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A snake moves forward on rough ground mainly by
questions.A: walking on the tips of its ribs, which it uses like many short legs
questions.B: throwing its body into waves that push against irregularities of the ground
questions.C: jumping from place to place by straightening its body suddenly
questions.D: rolling over sideways down the slope of the ground
questions.explanation: Serpentine locomotion: the sides of the curves press against stones and plants, driving the snake forward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Paramecium moves through water by means of
questions.explanation: Thousands of tiny cilia beat in coordinated waves, driving the cell forward in a spiral path.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Euglena swims towards moderate light in a pond. This movement of the whole organism towards a stimulus is
questions.explanation: Taxes are locomotory responses of whole organisms; tropisms are growth responses of parts of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In mammals the pelvic girdle is firmly fused to the sacrum in order to
questions.B: transmit the thrust of the hind limbs to the body
questions.C: allow the hind limbs to rotate freely
questions.explanation: A rigid connection is needed because the hind legs provide most of the propulsive force in running.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The bones of the human arm from the shoulder to the elbow and from the elbow to the wrist are respectively the
questions.explanation: The humerus is the upper arm bone; the radius and ulna form the forearm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The bicuspid (mitral) valve of the heart prevents blood from flowing back from the
questions.A: right ventricle into the right atrium
questions.B: left ventricle into the left atrium
questions.D: pulmonary artery into the right ventricle
questions.explanation: The bicuspid valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle; the tricuspid valve is on the right side.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood returning from the body tissues enters the heart through the
questions.B: venae cavae into the right atrium
questions.C: pulmonary veins into the left atrium
questions.D: pulmonary artery into the right ventricle
questions.explanation: Deoxygenated blood from the body collects in the right atrium before being pumped to the lungs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In mammals the blood passes through the heart twice in each complete circuit of the body. An advantage of this double circulation is that
questions.A: the blood moves more slowly through the lungs and picks up more oxygen
questions.B: oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are kept separate and blood reaches the body at high pressure
questions.C: the heart needs only one ventricle to pump blood round the body
questions.D: the lungs receive blood at the same high pressure as the rest of the body
questions.explanation: Blood returning from the lungs is re-pumped by the powerful left ventricle before going to the tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pulse felt at the wrist is caused by
questions.A: blood flowing steadily through the veins of the wrist towards the heart
questions.B: the stretching and recoil of the artery wall each time the left ventricle contracts
questions.C: the contraction of the muscles of the wrist and hand when they move
questions.D: the movement of lymph along the lymph vessels of the arm
questions.explanation: The pulse rate therefore equals the heart rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A nurse records a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. The figure 120 represents the pressure when the
questions.explanation: Systolic pressure (120) occurs during ventricular contraction; diastolic pressure (80) during relaxation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Exchange of materials between the blood and the body cells takes place in the capillaries because capillaries
questions.A: carry blood at a very high pressure from the heart
questions.B: have walls one cell thick and blood flows through them slowly
questions.C: contain valves that hold the blood still for exchange
questions.D: have thick muscular walls that squeeze substances out
questions.explanation: Their thin walls, narrow bore and enormous total surface area allow rapid diffusion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A blood test of a patient with a bacterial infection would most likely show a rise in the number of
questions.explanation: White cells (phagocytes and lymphocytes) multiply to fight infection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is transported dissolved in the blood plasma?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is carried mainly by haemoglobin inside the red cells; food, wastes, hormones and most carbon(IV) oxide travel in the plasma.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The lymph nodes in the neck of a person with a throat infection become swollen because
questions.A: they fill with excess blood from the infected throat
questions.B: the lymphocytes in them multiply to fight the infection
questions.C: lymph stops flowing through them during the infection
questions.D: they store the bacteria until the infection is over
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes filter lymph and are sites of lymphocyte production and antibody formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man collapses with severe chest pain after a blockage of a coronary artery. His heart muscle is damaged because it
questions.A: receives too much oxygen through the remaining arteries
questions.B: is deprived of oxygen and glucose carried by that artery
questions.C: is filled with lymph that leaks from the blocked artery
questions.D: is squeezed by the lungs when the man breathes in deeply
questions.explanation: The coronary arteries supply the heart wall itself; a blocked branch causes a heart attack.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A yam tuber that grows underground is full of starch made from sugar produced in the leaves. The sugar reached the tuber through the
questions.explanation: Translocation of manufactured food takes place in the phloem, in any direction the plant needs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Sap oozes from the cut stump of a well-watered plant early in the morning. This is due to
questions.explanation: Active pumping of ions into the xylem by root cells draws water in by osmosis and pushes it up the stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Stomata open in the light because the guard cells
questions.B: take up water and become turgid, curving apart
questions.C: are pushed apart by the epidermal cells
questions.explanation: Their unevenly thickened walls make the turgid guard cells bend outwards, opening the pore.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Antibodies that destroy invading germs are produced by
questions.explanation: Lymphocytes make specific antibodies; phagocytes engulf germs directly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person of blood group AB can receive blood from donors of any ABO group because his plasma contains
questions.explanation: With no antibodies against A or B antigens, no donor red cells are agglutinated (universal recipient).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The hepatic portal vein carries blood
questions.A: from the liver back to the right side of the heart
questions.B: rich in absorbed food from the intestine to the liver
questions.C: rich in oxygen from the heart to the liver
questions.D: rich in urea from the kidneys to the liver
questions.explanation: The liver processes and stores the absorbed nutrients before they reach the general circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During a sickle-cell crisis a patient feels severe pain in the joints because
questions.A: the sickled red cells block small blood vessels and starve the tissues of oxygen
questions.B: the blood becomes too dilute to carry enough food to the joints
questions.C: too many white cells are produced and they crowd the joints
questions.D: the heart beats too slowly to push blood as far as the joints
questions.explanation: Rigid sickle-shaped cells cannot squeeze through capillaries, causing blockage and tissue damage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Amoeba does not need a transport system because
questions.A: it does not respire and so never needs a supply of oxygen
questions.B: its large surface area in relation to its volume lets diffusion supply all its needs
questions.C: it lives in water, which carries all its food and wastes for it
questions.D: it has a contractile vacuole that pumps substances round the cell
questions.explanation: In a single small cell no part is far from the surface; large multicellular organisms need blood systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The correct order of the groups used in classifying organisms, from the largest to the smallest, is
questions.A: kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
questions.B: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
questions.C: species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
questions.D: phylum, kingdom, class, family, order, genus, species
questions.explanation: Each kingdom is divided into phyla, phyla into classes, and so on down to species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the scientific name Homo sapiens, the word Homo is the
questions.explanation: The binomial system names the genus first (capital letter) and the species second.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A mushroom belongs to the kingdom
questions.explanation: Fungi lack chlorophyll and feed by absorbing digested organic matter; their walls contain chitin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bacteria that are spherical in shape are called
questions.explanation: Cocci are round, bacilli rod-shaped, spirilla spiral and vibrios comma-shaped.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A green thread-like organism from a pond shows a spiral, ribbon-shaped chloroplast in each cell. It is
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga named after its spiral chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An animal with three pairs of jointed legs, two pairs of wings and one pair of antennae is
questions.explanation: These are the defining features of the class Insecta.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A crayfish differs from an insect in having
questions.A: one pair of antennae and only three pairs of legs
questions.B: two pairs of antennae and more than three pairs of legs
questions.C: no exoskeleton covering its soft segmented body
questions.D: two pairs of wings and a body of three parts
questions.explanation: Crustaceans have two pairs of antennae and many limbs, and most live in water and breathe with gills.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An animal with a long body of many similar segments, each bearing two pairs of legs, is a
questions.explanation: Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment; centipedes have one pair and poison claws.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A whale lives in the sea and looks like a fish, yet it is classified as a mammal because it
questions.A: has fins and swims through the water like a fish
questions.B: breathes with lungs and suckles its young with milk
questions.C: lays soft eggs in the water like most fishes
questions.D: has a skeleton made of bone rather than cartilage
questions.explanation: Mammals have mammary glands, hair, lungs and a diaphragm and are warm-blooded.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The ostrich cannot fly, yet it is classified as a bird because it
questions.A: has a beak and feathers and lays hard-shelled eggs
questions.B: can run very fast on its two long legs
questions.C: is warm-blooded and has a four-chambered heart
questions.D: has two legs and stands upright like a man
questions.explanation: Feathers are found only in birds; warm blood and two legs are shared with other groups.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A shark differs from a tilapia in having
questions.A: a skeleton of bone and gills covered by an operculum
questions.B: a skeleton of cartilage and gill slits without an operculum
questions.C: a swim bladder that keeps it afloat in the water
questions.D: overlapping scales and paired fins on its body
questions.explanation: Sharks and rays are cartilaginous fishes; tilapia and most other fishes are bony.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A groundnut plant has net-veined leaves, two cotyledons in each seed and a tap root. It is classified as a
questions.explanation: Dicotyledons also have flower parts in fours or fives and vascular bundles arranged in a ring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The brown dots found in rows on the underside of a fern frond are
questions.explanation: Ferns reproduce by spores released from sporangia grouped in sori.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The malaria parasite Plasmodium is classified as a protozoan because it
questions.A: is a single cell with a true nucleus
questions.B: is a single cell without a nucleus
questions.C: is a virus that lives inside red cells
questions.D: is made of many cells with nuclei
questions.explanation: Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotes; bacteria have no true nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A virus can reproduce only
questions.explanation: Viruses have no cytoplasm or ribosomes; they use the host cell's machinery to make new virus particles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An unsegmented, cylindrical worm about 20 cm long, pointed at both ends and found in the human intestine, is
questions.explanation: Ascaris lumbricoides is a nematode; tapeworms are flat and segmented, earthworms are segmented annelids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The shell of a snail is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The mantle is a fold of the body wall that lays down the calcium carbonate shell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The earthworm is placed in the phylum Annelida because it has
questions.A: a hard shell and a large muscular foot for creeping
questions.B: a body divided into ring-like segments with bristles (chaetae)
questions.C: jointed legs and a hard exoskeleton made of chitin
questions.D: a flat, unsegmented body with a mouth on the underside
questions.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms; the chaetae grip the soil during burrowing.
